description: What this repository must look like. The SDK is written at Stigg and copied in; a copied file keeps its path, and a handful are rewritten on the way. These are the invariants that hold here, and tools/repo-tests enforces every one of them.

values.scripts.build: rimraf dist && tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json

package.json.why: Nothing is released from here, so the publishing fields are absent and `private` stays. `main` and `typings` point at `src`, as they do at the source.

tsconfig.json.why: Self-contained: the compiler options the source is written against, inlined, with no workspace paths to redirect. `tools/**` is this repository's own addition.

test/docs-contract.test.ts.rewrite: the document list filters for what is present, because `docs/instances.md` is not here; and the forbidden-term list keeps only the terms a reader here can act on
test/docs-contract.test.ts.why: A missing document would otherwise throw and fail the suite. The filter is a no-op once the document arrives. The dropped terms are spellings that only exist where this package is written, and naming them to ban them would be the one place they appear.

.env.template.why: A template shipping defaults invites someone to keep them. The guide documents each variable and its default, and the examples compile their own.

docs/**.why: The guide is written in a monorepo, where a script is `yarn workspace <package> run <name>`. Here the package is the repository, so the same line is `yarn <name>` - and nothing may name `docs/instances.md`, which this repository deliberately does not have.

absent-documents.what: references to a document `paths.absent` lists are dropped, or pointed at the one that is here
